clue.text: Arrived with plenty where the knights were

parts.note: arrived means came
a lot is plenty

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with lots of supplies at the knights' quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's legendary court, seat of the Round Table, is where his knights gathered.

clue.text: Bird to tip up part of the 'plane

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is stood on its head and read bottom to top

parts.note: tip taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird tilts upward a section of the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIP into PIT under COCK. The apostrophe in 'plane marks the old short form of aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilot's compartment at the front of an aircraft is a section of the machine.

clue.text: New names for churchman's place

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters of names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minister moves into a home under fresh names.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's official residence, especially in Scotland, is the clergyman's house.

clue.text: Wind instruments don't begin to become stringed ones…

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: flutes are wind instruments

explanation.surface: Woodwind players are told their instruments should turn into string ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't begin' removes the F of FLUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucked instruments with strings, played like an old guitar, are the 'ones' with strings.

clue.text: And Heavens, the noise they make!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'By Jove!' or 'Good heavens!'
the rumbling the skies make in a storm

explanation.definitionFit: As an oath it expresses astonishment; as a sound it is the crash of a storm overhead.

clue.text: Lights a box holding them in a book, sometimes

definitions.text: Lights a box holding them in a book, sometimes

parts.words: Lights a box holding them in a book, sometimes
parts.note: things to strike fire with, kept in a box or sometimes in a folded card book

explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks for lighting fires come in boxes or in little card booklets.

clue.text: Steam is curling round the painter

indicators.note: steam curling round is twisted out of shape, so the letters of steam is are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vapour wreathes about an artist at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steam' looks like the subject of the surface, but it is anagram fodder; 'curling round' is the signal, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leading figure of Fauvism.

clue.text: Checks on the sky? No, in it!

definitions.text: Checks on the sky? No, in it!

parts.words: Checks on the sky? No, in it!
parts.note: not someone studying the heavens from below, but someone who puts new aircraft through trials up in the air

explanation.definitionFit: An aviator who flies new aircraft to check their performance does checking in the sky.

clue.text: Contest that sometimes involves jumping, of course

definitions.text: Contest that sometimes involves jumping, of course

parts.words: Contest that sometimes involves jumping, of course
parts.note: a competition run on a course, with jumps over fences in steeplechases

explanation.definitionFit: A contest between mounts on a turf course sometimes includes fences to leap.

clue.text: Entertainers of an airy kind?

parts.note: airs are tunes, so entertainers dealing in airs are vocal performers

explanation.definitionFit: Vocal performers deliver airs, meaning songs or tunes.

clue.text: Pull down what's opposite!

parts.note: the opposite of demolishing a building is putting one up

explanation.definitionFit: Building something up is the reverse of demolishing it.

clue.text: Fascinating woman sounds alarming

definitions.meaning: a seductive, alluring temptress, after the singing nymphs of Greek myth who lured sailors
a device that sounds a warning wail

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical temptress gave her name to the wailing alarm on police cars and factories.

clue.text: The French speed out, delighted

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
taken as written

explanation.surface: French drivers racing away look happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LA plus SPEED into PLEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and happy are synonyms of delighted.

clue.text: Most excellent Soviet sacrifice-both can accompany it

definitions.text: Most excellent Soviet sacrifice-both can accompany it

parts.words: Most excellent Soviet sacrifice-both can accompany it
parts.note: a word meaning best of all, which goes in front of Soviet (the USSR's parliament) and sacrifice (giving one's life)

explanation.definitionFit: Highest or greatest in quality, and the first word of the phrases with Soviet and sacrifice.

clue.text: It's a job to compel this group of fighting men!.

parts.note: a task is a job
to force is to compel

explanation.surface: Ordering soldiers about is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit assembled for a specific operation is a group of fighting men.

clue.text: Sort of weapon that gives us the vapours!

definitions.text: Sort of weapon that gives us the vapours!

parts.words: Sort of weapon that gives us the vapours!
parts.note: the vapours is an old fit of faintness, but here it is literal fumes released by a device

explanation.definitionFit: A device thrown to release a screening cloud is a weapon that emits vapour.

clue.text: Bewitch one? Can, if tea's stirred

indicators.note: tea that is stirred is mixed up, so the letters of can if tea's are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the possessive gives the letters TEAS

explanation.surface: Someone offers a cuppa as a charm to win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or captivate someone is to cast a spell over them.

clue.text: And they're burdensome -so gets weapons ready

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means heavy burdens; as a verb it means charges a gun.

clue.text: Ways through locks on them, quite often

definitions.text: Ways through locks on them, quite often

parts.words: Ways through locks on them, quite often
parts.note: entrances that often have locks fitted, not canal locks

explanation.definitionFit: Hinged entrances to rooms are ways through, and usually carry locks.

clue.text: No-one can hope to do this

definitions.text: No-one can hope to do this

parts.words: No-one can hope to do this
parts.note: the act of giving up all hope cannot be done while one is still hoping

explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is the opposite of hoping.

clue.text: Generally found in palatial surroundings!

parts.note: people usually found at a royal palace, attending the monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Attendants at a royal court are found in palaces.

clue.text: Pole-he's Common Market mad concerning dairy produce

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters HES
EEC, the European Economic Community, was known as the Common Market
S stands for south, one of the poles

explanation.surface: A Polish man is furious about European dairy rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges HES plus EEC into CHEESE, and S for Pole goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar, brie and the like are products made from milk.

clue.text: Sheer honesty characterises one who is

definitions.text: Sheer honesty characterises one who is

parts.words: Sheer honesty characterises one who is
parts.note: sheer means vertical, and an honest person is described as standing straight in character

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both vertical, like a sheer cliff, and honest.

clue.text: The police think he's wrongdoer, possibly

definitions.text: The police think he's wrongdoer, possibly

parts.words: The police think he's wrongdoer, possibly
parts.note: a person the police believe may have committed a crime

explanation.definitionFit: A person believed possibly guilty of a crime is under police suspicion.

clue.text: Barren monster I leave within

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the words monster I leave

explanation.surface: A fearsome creature says it will depart from the empty interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to produce offspring or crops means infertile.

clue.text: Leaves a job concerning portents

parts.note: re means about or concerning
signs are portents or omens

explanation.surface: Someone quits work because of omens.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a post is to leave employment.

clue.text: Sharp part of a plant

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sharp part of a plant (5)' does not fit GRAVE (it suits THORN); clues seem misplaced, with 23-down and 25-across missing

clue.text: Stick sweet in it

parts.note: sugar is a sweet substance
a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: A cane with sweetness inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall grass whose stalks hold sugar is a stick with sweetness inside.

clue.text: If pressed to do so, they will give us clean sheets!

definitions.text: If pressed to do so, they will give us clean sheets!

parts.words: If pressed to do so, they will give us clean sheets!
parts.note: not laundry presses but erasers pressed on paper to clean the pages

explanation.definitionFit: Erasers rubbed on paper leave the sheets clean.

clue.text: He and I leave the empties broken, causing a storm

indicators.note: leave says the letters of he and I are taken away from the pool
broken means the letters of the empties are shattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters to be broken up
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people abandon smashed bottles in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' removes H, E and I from THE EMPTIES, and 'broken' rearranges what remains, TEMPTES, into TEMPEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent windstorm is a storm.
